title: Evidence Aggregation Agent - Oncall Playbook and Operational Runbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This runbook is the operational playbook for the Evidence Aggregation Agent (EAA) — the service responsible for collecting, normalizing, deduplicating, and exporting control evidence and audit events to downstream systems (SIEM, evidence-lake, compliance archive). It covers day-to-day operations, triage flows for common failure modes, SIEM export contract details, and RBAC v2 interaction patterns relevant to oncall and engineering rotations.

Audience:
- Security & Compliance oncall engineers
- Observability / SRE engineers who support evidence pipelines
- Product engineers implementing new evidence producers

High-level architecture summary (one-paragraph):
EAA runs in a distributed fleet with per-region collectors that pull or subscribe to event streams from producers (runtime-control-plane, auth gateway, infra agents). Events are mapped into a canonical audit schema, checked for TTL/retention labels, optionally hashed for proof-of-append, and written to the evidence buffer. A reliable exporter batches evidence to SIEMs with explicit sequence numbers and acknowledgements. A separate export-checkpointer persists offsets into the proofchain storage. RBAC v2 gates are applied at ingest-time to redact or drop sensitive fields when tenant policies require it.

Key concepts and terminology:
- Event envelope: single transport unit from producer to EAA; contains raw_payload, producer_id, timestamp, signature_meta
- Canonical audit event (v2): normalized record with fields listed below
- Proofchain: append-only chain of per-tenant hashes used for later attestation
- Export batch: ordered list of canonical events with batch_id, sequence_range, checksum

Canonical audit event (v2) required fields (recommended mapping):
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
- tenant_id (string)
- request_id (string)
- actor_id (string) // user/service performing action
- actor_type (string) // user | service | system
- action (string) // e.g., "model.deploy", "key.rotate", "route.call"
- resource_type (string) // e.g., model, key, route
- resource_id (string)
- outcome (string) // success | failure | partial
- client_ip (string, optional)
- outcome_detail (string, optional)
- bytes_transferred (int, optional)
- event_hash (hex string) // SHA256 of canonical serialized event for proofchain
- ingestion_node_id (string) // collector instance id
- schema_version (string) // e.g., "audit.v2"
- redaction_profile (string) // which RBAC redaction was applied, if any

(Notes: keep events small. If payloads are large, attach payload_ref to evidence-lake rather than embed.)

RBAC v2 interactions (ingest-side behaviors):
- Ingest checks tenant policy caches; three possible actions per-field: keep, redact (replace with <REDACTED:reason>), drop (remove field).
- If RBAC cache TTL expired, collector falls back to read-only cached policy and tags event with redaction_profile="policy-cache-stale" then emits a telemetry counter.
- Permission denied at ingest (producer not allowed to emit): event is either rejected (with NACK to producer) or routed to quarantine bucket depending on policy. Oncall should verify quarantine size and run sample replays.

SIEM export contract (operational summary):
- Delivery semantics: at-least-once by default; exporters provide idempotency keys in headers and include event_hash to detect dupes.
- Batch format: JSONL envelope with batch_id (uuid), seq_start, seq_end, batch_checksum (SHA256), region, producer_version, schema_version.
- Acknowledgement: SIEM must respond with 200 + minimal ack payload {batch_id, accepted_count}. Retries are exponential backoff (base 2) with jitter; persistent failure after 6 attempts moves batch to backfill queue and triggers alert.
- Backfill mode: backfill queue supports prioritized replay, and each replay increments a replay_counter on event metadata.
- Export throttling: exporters observe downstream 429/503 hints and switch to prioritized-mode honoring control-plane priority tags.

Common failure modes and triage steps (oncall):
1) Missing events for tenant X (symptom: dashboard per-tenant event-rate drops >60% for 10m)
   - Check collector health dashboard: CPU, mem, last-heartbeat (observability link in header).
   - Check ingestion offsets vs producer: run `eaactl offsets --tenant X --region us-west-2` to view lags.
   - If lag exists: identify whether producer is publishing by checking producer logs (link provided in linked_artifacts). If producer healthy, escalate to infra team to check network ACLs.
   - If collector stalled: restart single instance using canary restart: `kubectl -n sec-eaa rollout restart deployment/eaa-collector -l az=canary` then monitor offsets.

2) Duplicate events / export dupes (symptom: SIEM reports duplicate request_ids)
   - Verify batch checksum mismatches and search for repeated event_hash values.
   - Check exporter idempotency header generation code (PR link in linked_artifacts). If recent deploy, consider rollback to previous container image tag.
   - If duplicates are from replays, consult backfill-replay logs for overlapping seq ranges and adjust replay window to avoid overlap.

3) Schema drift / validation failures (symptom: validation_errors counter spikes)
   - Run schema diff tool: `eaactl schema-diff --producer P --sample 100`
   - If drift expected from product change, coordinate with product owner to publish migration mapping. If unexpected, quarantine example events and create JIRA issue JIRA-SEC-2148 (linked).

4) SIEM export failures (symptom: exporter in 5xx or non-ack state)
   - Check exporter logs and SIEM response headers.
   - If 401/403: confirm service principal keys are present in secrets manager and not rotated. For RBAC v2 related 403s, verify new permission scopes introduced in last deploy.
   - If persistent 5xx: escalate to GTM integration contact and open a support ticket with SIEM vendor including batch_id and representative event samples (redact PII).

5) Proofchain mismatch (symptom: hash mismatch detected during attestation run)
   - Stop new appends for effected tenant ID to preserve chain state.
   - Run proofchain verify tool: `proofcheck --tenant T --from seqA --to seqB`.
   - If mismatch found, determine earliest divergent sequence and replay from nearest consistent snapshot. Notify compliance and legal teams per incident classification.

Operational checks and smoke tests (daily/weekly):
- Daily:
  - verify collector heartbeats across regions (>= 99% in last 24h)
  - sample 100 events across tenants and validate schema_version == "audit.v2"
  - ensure export success rate >= 99.5% in last 24h
- Weekly:
  - run a dry-run backfill of 10k events to test replay path
  - rotate service principal keys in a staging environment to validate secret rotation playbook

Oncall escalation matrix (first 30 minutes to resolve):
- Primary oncall: security-compliance-oncall (Slack: #sec-eaa-oncall)
- Secondary: observability-sre (individual: Miguel Torres)
- Pager escalation: Infra platform oncall if network or node outage suspected
- Exec notice: Compliance lead (Aisha Patel) if proofchain or retention SLA is violated

Operational runbook snippets (commands):
- offsets check: `eaactl offsets --tenant $TENANT --region $REGION`
- verify export status: `kubectl -n sec-eaa logs deploy/eaa-exporter --since=1h | grep "batch_id=$BATCH"`
- replay batch: `eaactl replay --batch $BATCH --priority manual`

Alerting thresholds (recommended):
- per-tenant ingest drop: 60% drop sustained for 10m -> P2 alert
- exporter consecutive failures > 6 attempts -> P1 alert
- proofchain verify mismatch -> P0 (immediate legal/exec notify)
- RBAC cache stale > 30m -> P2 alert and telemetry tag

Testing guidance for engineers (pre-merge checklist when modifying EAA):
- unit tests for schema mappings and redaction logic
- end-to-end test that produces an event and asserts it lands in SIEM dev workspace with correct redaction_profile tag
- add load test demonstrating bounded memory and batch sizes at 2x expected peak
- update the linked_artifacts references and add migration notes when changing canonical fields

Retention, TTL, and compliance notes:
- Event TTL is applied at ingest-time; retention labels (retention=7y|1y|90d) must be present. Shorter retention can be applied by governance policies.
- All PII-containing payloads must be redacted or referenced via payload_ref. Do NOT store raw user content in evidence-buckets unless encrypted-at-rest and explicitly cleared in retention policy.

Post-incident & postmortem checklist:
- Create JIRA and link to incident timeline
- Export representative sample of failing events (redacted)
- Run proofchain verify script and attach signed summary to the ticket
- Update runbook with new mitigation steps discovered during the incident

Maintenance tasks and run cadence:
- Monthly: rotate exporter certificates in staging and validate handshake with SIEM
- Quarterly: run full proofchain attestation for top 10 tenants by volume
- Biannual: review RBAC v2 policy cache TTL and evaluate policy cache distribution strategy

Appendix: sample minimal audit.v2 JSON (single-line):
{"timestamp_utc":"2026-01-20T15:04:05Z","tenant_id":"t-12345","request_id":"req-9f3a","actor_id":"svc-ingress","actor_type":"service","action":"route.invoke","resource_type":"route","resource_id":"r-33","outcome":"success","ingestion_node_id":"collector-usw-02","event_hash":"3a7f..."}

Notes and outstanding work (todo):
- Formalize SLAs with SIEM partners for batching windows and outage RTOs (owner: Aisha)
- Add test harness to simulate RBAC policy rotations and validate redaction fallbacks (owner: Ravi)
- Design a low-cost cold-storage for long-tail backfill requests (owner: Sofia)

Contact list (runbook owners):
- Runbook owner: Lena Chen (lena@redwood.com)
- Oncall lead: Miguel Torres (miguel@redwood.com)
- Compliance contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.com)

This document is intentionally operational-first: include it in runbook rotations and update after any incident. Keep examples and commands current in linked_artifacts.
